sections.name: I. INTRODUCTION
sentences: Plaintiff, Joelle Burgess (“Plaintiff”), brings this action against her employer, GlaxoSmithKline LLC (“Defendant”), for discriminating and retaliating against Plaintiff based upon her age, in violation of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, as amended, 29 U.S.C. § 621, et seq. (“ADEA”), and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, as amended, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq. (“PHRA”).
Plaintiff seeks damages, including back pay, front pay, compensatory damages, liquidated damages, attorneys’ fees and costs, and all other relief that this Court deems appropriate.

sections.name: II. PARTIES
sentences: Plaintiff is an individual and a citizen of Pennsylvania.
Plaintiff resides in Trappe, Pennsylvania.
Plaintiff was born in 1969.
Plaintiff is currently fifty-three (53) years of age. Plaintiff was fifty-two (52) years of age when Defendant terminated her employment on January 13, 2022.
Defendant is engaged in an industry affecting interstate commerce and regularly does business in Pennsylvania.

Prior to Plaintiff’s January 2022 termination, Plaintiff worked primarily at Defendant’s corporate office located at 1250 S Collegeville Road, Collegeville, Pennsylvania At all relevant times, Defendant employed twenty (20) or more employees.

At all times material hereto, Defendant acted by and through its authorized agents, servants, workmen, and/or employees acting within the course and scope of their employment with Defendant and in furtherance of Defendant’s business.
At all times material hereto, Defendant acted as an “Employer” within the meaning of the statutes that form the basis of the matter.
At all times material hereto, Plaintiff was an “Employee” of Defendant within the meaning of the statutes that form the basis of the matter.

sections.name: III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE
sentences: The causes of action that form the basis of the matter arise under the ADEA and the PHRA.
The District Court has jurisdiction over Count I (ADEA) pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1331.
The District Court has jurisdiction over Count II (PHRA) pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1367.
Venue is proper in this District Court under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) because a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claims occurred within this District.

On or about March 14, 2022, Plaintiff filed a Complaint of Discrimination with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (“PHRC”) and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”) complaining of the acts of discrimination alleged herein (the “Complaint of Discrimination”).
Attached hereto, incorporated herein, and marked as Exhibit 1 is a true and correct copy of Plaintiff’s Complaint of Discrimination (with personal identifying information redacted).
On November 16, 2022, the EEOC issued Plaintiff a Notice of Right to Sue regarding her Complaint of Discrimination.
Attached hereto, incorporated herein, and marked as Exhibit 2 is a true and correct copy of the notice (with personal identifying information redacted).
Plaintiff has fully complied with all administrative prerequisites for the commencement of this action.

sections.name: IV. FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
sentences: Plaintiff was hired by Defendant in July 19901 and as of her termination had more than thirty-one (31) years of service with the company.
Plaintiff consistently performed her job duties in a highly competent manner and received positive feedback.

Plaintiff last held the position of Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. Plaintiff last reported to Steven Knight (572), Scientific Team Director, Grade 5. Knight reported to Andy Peat (52), Section Director, Grade 4. Peat reported to Paul Coleman (50), Head of Medicinal Chemistry.
All dates contained herein are approximations.
All ages herein are approximations.
In January 2020, Plaintiff began indirectly reporting to Coleman, when he was hired as Head of Medical Chemistry.

In or about January 2020, Defendant hired Sophia Robinson (30), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. In or about January 2020, Defendant hired Martin Rauch (30), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. On or about May 1, 2021, Plaintiff began reporting to Knight.

In or about June 2021, Defendant hired Xavier Riart-Ferrer (30), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. In or about July 2021, Defendant hired Amberly Sanford (30), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. In or about August 2021, Defendant hired Hannah Shenouda (28), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. In or about September 2021, Defendant hired Tessa Lynch-Colanneta (30), Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7. On October 20, 2021, in a meeting entitled “Transforming Medicinal Chemistry,” attended by Human Resources and Global Medicinal Chemistry employees, Defendant announced that thirteen (13) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees would be terminated.
Defendant had hired six (6) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees within less than the last two (2) years.

On October 26, 2021, in a meeting attended by Human Resources and Global Medicinal Chemistry employees, Defendant stated that Global Medicinal Chemistry employees would be evaluated to determine which employees would retain their positions and remain employed with Defendant and which employees would be terminated.

On or about November 3, 2021, in a meeting with Peat, Plaintiff asked, and stated that she did not understand, why Defendant was terminating thirteen (13) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees when Defendant had hired six (6) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees within the last two (2) years, all of whom were approximately thirty (30) years old. Plaintiff complained that Defendant’s reduction in force appeared to her and others in the department that Coleman, on behalf of Defendant, was pushing out the experienced Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees that were age fifty (50) and older after hiring younger Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees.
Peat agreed that it appeared that Coleman was pushing to terminate older employees.

Peat stated that the department’s reorganization was not for budgetary reasons or because consumer products was demerging from Defendant in 2022, as no other department was undergoing a reduction in force.

On or about November 8, 2021, in a meeting with Beth Knapp-Reed (46), Scientific Director, Plaintiff asked, and stated that she did not understand, why Defendant was terminating thirteen (13) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees when Defendant had hired six (6) Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees within the last two (2) years, all of whom were approximately thirty (30) years old. Plaintiff complained that Defendant’s reduction in force appeared to her and others in the department that Coleman, on behalf of Defendant, was pushing out the experienced Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees that were age fifty (50) and older after hiring younger Investigator, Medical Chemistry, Grade 7 employees.
Plaintiff stated that she did not understand why she had to be reevaluated to retain her position and remain employed with Defendant.
Knapp-Reed responded that she did not know what Coleman’s reasons were for the reduction in force and reevaluation process, and that Coleman and Human Resources should answer these questions.
On December 1, 2021, in a meeting with Knight, Plaintiff stated that she wanted to remain employed with Defendant for many more years.

Plaintiff was told that, as part of the confidential reevaluation process, to determine which employees in the department would be retained and which would be terminated, Knight and Knapp-Reed would present Plaintiff to the decision-making panel.
On January 13, 2022, in a virtual meeting with Peat, Defendant notified Plaintiff that her employment would be terminated, effective March 5, 2022.
Plaintiff was provided no explanation for her termination.
Plaintiff was only told that she would not be retained as an employee.
On January 13, 2022, following the above, in an email from Peat, Defendant notified Plaintiff that her employment would be terminated, effective March 5, 2022.
The email did not provide any explanation for Plaintiff’s termination.
On January 13, 2022, Defendant terminated Knight (57), effective March 5, 2022.
On January 13, 2022, Defendant terminated Peat (52), effective March 5, 2022.

On January 28, 2022, in a meeting with Bryan King (50), Scientific Director, Plaintiff stated that she did not understand why she was terminated, and that she was disappointed that Coleman, on behalf of Defendant, terminated so many employees over age fifty (50).

King did not deny that age was a factor in the termination process, and acknowledged that all of the six (6), young, newly-hired Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7 employees had retained their jobs.
On January 28, 2022, following the above, in a meeting with Knight, Plaintiff asked what her “score” was in the process that Defendant allegedly used to reevaluate and terminate employees.
Knight refused to tell Plaintiff her score, and stated that Defendant would not allow him to disclose this information.
Plaintiff stated that it appeared that Coleman terminated employees over age fifty (50) and retained the younger, newly hired employees.
Defendant terminated Plaintiff’s employment because of her age and/or her age discrimination complaints.
Defendant offered no explanation, including the selection criteria, as to why Plaintiff, in particular, was terminated while younger, less-experienced and/or less-qualified employees were retained.
Defendant assigned Plaintiff’s job duties to substantially-younger employees.
Plaintiff was more qualified to perform her job duties than the substantially-younger employees to whom her job duties were assigned.
Plaintiff received positive performance reviews throughout her more than thirty- one (31) years of service with Defendant.
Plaintiff had no disciplinary or performance issues throughout her more than thirty- one (31) years of service with Defendant.
Defendant did not offer Plaintiff a downgraded position or a position with reduced pay in lieu of termination.
According to the OWBPA list, in addition to Plaintiff, the following employees holding an Investigator, Grade 7 position were terminated when Plaintiff was terminated.
Israel Pendrak (65); Dominic Suarez (60); Hong Nie (57); Hongxing Yan (54); Huijie Li (52); Jenny Zhang (51); Brent McCleland (50); and Mike Squire (43).
All Investigator, Grade 7 employees, except for one (1), who were terminated when Plaintiff was terminated, were age fifty (50) or older.
According to the OWBPA list, the following substantially younger employees holding an Investigator, Grade 7 position were retained when Plaintiff was terminated.
All Investigator, Grade 7 employees under age forty (40) were retained when Plaintiff was terminated.
According to the OWBPA list, the following employees holding an Investigator, Medicinal Chemistry, Grade 7 position were retained when Plaintiff was terminated.
Plaintiff was more qualified for these employees’ positions.
Defendant retained at least twenty-seven (27) less-qualified, substantially-younger employees in positions for which Plaintiff was more qualified.

At Defendant, employees are eligible for retirement benefits, including subsidized health insurance, when they have an age plus years of service combination of seventy-five (75) or are age fifty-five (55) with ten (10) years of service.
Employees commented that Plaintiff was eligible for retirement benefits at Defendant.
Defendant has a Future Leaders graduate program, and provides development, training, and leadership opportunities to young employees.
Defendant does not provide the same or similar opportunities, development and training to older employees.
The Future Leaders graduate program intentionally discriminates against employees over age forty (40) and disparately impacts employees over age forty (40).
Defendant targets and provides financial incentives to older employees to leave the workforce.
Defendant does not target or provide financial incentives to younger employees to leave the workforce.
Defendant’s conduct evidences a bias against older employees and a preference for younger employees.
Defendant’s conduct evidences a bias against employees who engage in protected activity.
Defendant’s age discriminatory and retaliatory conduct has caused Plaintiff emotional distress.
Defendant’s retaliatory conduct would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining of discrimination.

sections.name: (VIOLATION OF THE ADEA)
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates the paragraphs above as if set forth herein in their entirety.
By committing the foregoing acts of discrimination and retaliation against Plaintiff, Defendant violated the ADEA.
Defendant’s violation of the ADEA was intentional and willful under the circumstances, warranting the imposition of liquidated damages.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendant’s violation of the ADEA, Plaintiff has sustained the injuries, damages, and losses set forth herein and has incurred attorneys’ fees and costs.

Plaintiff is now suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable injury and monetary damages as a result of Defendant’s discriminatory and retaliatory acts unless and until this Court grants the relief requested herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

sections.name: (VIOLATION OF THE PHRA)
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates the paragraphs above as if set forth herein in their entirety.
By committing the foregoing acts of discrimination and retaliation against Plaintiff, Defendant violated the PHRA.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendant’s violation of the PHRA, Plaintiff has sustained the injuries, damages, and losses set forth herein and has incurred attorneys’ fees and costs.

Plaintiff is now suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable injury and monetary damages as a result of Defendant’s discriminatory and retaliatory acts unless and until this Court grants the relief requested herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

sections.name: RELIEF
sentences: WHEREFORE, Plaintiff seeks damages and legal and equitable relief in connection with Defendant’s unlawful conduct, and specifically prays that the Court grant the following relief to the Plaintiff by: a. declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be a violation of the ADEA and PHRA; b. enjoining and restraining permanently the violations alleged herein; c. awarding Plaintiff damages for back pay, front pay, and pre- and post- judgment interest; d. awarding compensatory damages to Plaintiff for past and future emotional distress and pain and suffering; e. awarding liquidated damages under the ADEA; f. awarding Plaintiff the costs of this action, together with reasonable attorneys’ fees; g. awarding Plaintiff such other damages as are appropriate under the ADEA and PHRA; and h. granting such other and further relief as this Court deems appropriate.
Respectfully submitted,.

sections.name: UNNAMED
sentences: This is a complaint filed by the plaintiff against their employer, alleging age discrimination and retaliation under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA) and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act (PHRA). The complaint outlines various incidents of alleged discriminatory behavior, including:.
Termination: The plaintiff was terminated from their position as an Investigator, Grade 7, along with several other employees over the age of 50.
Lack of explanation: The plaintiff claims that they were not provided with a valid reason for their termination and that younger, less-experienced employees were retained in similar positions.
Retaliation: The plaintiff alleges that they were retaliated against for complaining about age discrimination within the company.
Bias against older employees: The complaint suggests that the defendant has a bias against older employees and provides financial incentives to encourage them to leave the workforce.

The plaintiff is seeking damages, including back pay, front pay, pre- and post-judgment interest, compensatory damages for emotional distress and pain and suffering, liquidated damages under the ADEA, and attorneys' fees. They are also requesting that the court declare the defendant's actions a violation of the ADEA and PHRA and permanently enjoin the defendant from engaging in similar conduct in the future.
The complaint is supported by various exhibits, including:.
The OWBPA list: This document appears to be a list of employees who were terminated or retained within the company.
Performance reviews: The plaintiff claims that they received positive performance reviews throughout their employment with the defendant.
Retirement benefits: The complaint suggests that the defendant has a policy of providing retirement benefits to employees when they reach certain age and service milestones.
The complaint is filed by Console Mattiacci Law, LLC, on behalf of the plaintiff.
